newsitem.title: USA: Meredith to buy four TV stations for $435 million.
newsitem.headline: Meredith to buy four TV stations for $435 million.

text.p: Meredith Corp. said Friday it agreed to buy four TV stations from First Media Television, a partnership controlled by the Marriott family, for $75 million in cash and the assumption of $360 million in debt.

Meredith, which already owns seven TV stations, publishes Better Homes and Gardens, Ladies Home Journal and other magazines. The stations being acquired are in Orlando, Fla., Portland and Bend, Ore., and Greenville, S.C.
"Acquisition of the First Media television stations is a major step toward fulfilling our broadcasting growth strategy," Chief Executive Officer William Kerr said.
The purchase comes after Meredith exited a money-losing cable TV business last October by selling its stake in a cable system in Minneapolis and St. Paul for proceeds of $125 million.
The Des Moines, Iowa-based company was founded as a magazine publisher in 1902 and entered the television broadcasting business in 1948.

Since Meredith already owns a broadcast station in Orlando, WOFL-TV, affiliated with the Fox network, it said it would have to sell that station or the station to be acquired in Orlando to conform with federal rules on media ownership.
"Our desire is to own one of the Orlando stations and trade one of them for one or more stations with high growth opportunities," Kerr said.
Federal Communications Commission rules prohibit ownership of more than one television station in a single market.

The acquisition would mean Meredith's stations reach 8 percent of the nation's households, up from 5 percent, assuming it trades one of the Orlando stations for another in a market serving a similar number of households, it said.

The acquisition will hurt earnings per share in fiscal 1998 and 1999, Meredith said, worrying investors and driving its stock as low as $52, though it later recovered somewhat and was off 75 cents at $52.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
It said the deal would boost earnings starting in fiscal 2000. In the year ended last June, it earned $53.9 million, or $1.91 a share, on sales of $867.1 million.
Meredith on Wednesday said earnings rose 6 percent in its second quarter, paced by a strength in magazine publishing and broadcasting. Book publishing operating profits fell.
Earnings from continuing operations rose to $17.1 million, or 61 cents a share, in the quarter, from $16.1 million, or 57 cents a share. Sales fell 3 percent to $209.8 million.

The stations being acquired are CBS affiliate WCPX in Orlando, KPDX serving Portland, Ore., and Vancouver, Wash., KFXO in Bend, Ore., and WHNS serving Greenville and Asheville. The latter three are Fox network affiliates.
